title: U.S. House · Florida's 17th District
area: Southwest Florida's inland counties, including DeSoto, Hardee, Glades, Highlands, Okeechobee, and parts of Charlotte and Polk counties, under Florida's 2026 congressional map.

context.text: Florida's U.S. House elections use a new congressional map for 2026; Gov. Ron DeSantis signed the new district boundaries into law on May 4, 2026.
Incumbent Rep. Greg Steube (R) ran unopposed and his Republican primary was canceled. Matthew Montavon won the Democratic primary on August 18, 2026, defeating Allen Spence.

candidates.name: Greg Steube

summary.text: Greg Steube is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for the 17th District, in office since January 2019. He is an attorney and Army veteran who previously served in the Florida House and Senate.

background.text: Born in Manatee County, Florida; earned his bachelor's and law degrees from the University of Florida.
Served as an airborne infantry officer and judge advocate general in the U.S. Army, 2004–2008.
Served in the Florida House of Representatives (2010–2016) and Florida State Senate (2016–2018) before winning election to the U.S. House in 2018.

priorities.text: Veterans: says he is committed to supporting veterans, including through legislation to provide health care choices outside the VA system.
priorities.quote: I’ve spearheaded Congressional reform efforts to provide veterans with health care choices outside of the VA system through my landmark legislation, The Veterans’ True Choice Act.

priorities.text: Border and immigration: says the border must be secured by completing the wall and enforcing existing immigration laws.
priorities.quote: We must secure the border by completing the wall, and we must actually enforce the law so that illegal aliens are not rewarded for illegally crossing the border.

priorities.text: Agriculture: says he supports reducing regulatory burdens on farmers, ranchers and producers and creating fair trade markets for them.
priorities.quote: I maintain a firm stance against burdensome regulations in the agricultural sector, and support policies that help create fair trade markets for American farmers.

positions.summary: Says he has supported legislation protecting the right to self-defense and opposes efforts he says would infringe on that right.
positions.quote: Throughout my tenure in Congress, I have supported legislation that protects our God-given right to self-defense, and I oppose any efforts that infringe upon these rights and violate the Constitution.

positions.summary: Says he is fighting for policies to increase domestic energy production and opposes federal electric-vehicle mandates.
positions.quote: I am fighting for policies in Congress that reduce dependency on foreign nations, increase domestic energy production, and other means to make energy more affordable for Americans. I oppose the Biden-Harris Administration’s Electric Vehicle mandates and their wasteful taxpayer spending on EV charging infrastructure.

positions.summary: Describes himself as a defender of the right to life, welcomes state laws restricting abortion after the Supreme Court decision, and supports the Hyde Amendment.
positions.quote: I am a staunch defender of the right to life, and I am pleased that many states have sought to protect this right after the Supreme Court correctly decided that the Constitution did not prohibit states from acting to protect the lives of the unborn.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means (Health and Trade subcommittees) and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence for the 2025–2026 Congress.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and priorities are drawn from Steube's official House issues pages, which cover only a subset of the 15 tracked issues.

summary.text: Matthew Montavon is a Democratic candidate challenging incumbent Greg Steube. He spent 27 years working for the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization combating hunger and poverty, after service in the Peace Corps.

background.text: Born in South Bend, Indiana, into a family of nine children; worked odd jobs from high school through college to support himself.
Served in the Peace Corps and worked six years with local governments and national associations before 27 years with the UN Food and Agriculture Organization.
Currently serves as President of the Sarasota Democratic Hispanic Caucus and volunteer co-coordinator of the AARP Tax-Aide program.

priorities.text: Says he will work to fund government programs and expand public services including education, renewable energy transition, voting access, foreign aid, and civil rights protection.
Supports immigration reform to create a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers and long-term undocumented immigrants.

positions.summary: Says he would advocate eliminating ICE in its current form, limit detention to strict last-resort conditions, and create a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers and long-term undocumented immigrants.
positions.quote: advocating for the elimination of ICE in its current form and bring US immigration enforcement into line with international human rights standards. Detention should only be used under strict, limited conditions and as a measure of last resort.

positions.summary: Lists combating climate change among his policy passions and the transition to renewable energy among the public priorities he would fund.
Lists a woman's right to choose among his policy passions.
Says he wants to protect the Affordable Care Act, Medicare, and Medicaid in the short term while pushing for universal healthcare in the long term.

summary.text: Michael Quirk is running with no party affiliation in the general election for Florida's 17th District. No campaign website or detailed public statements were found.
